statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases a further point to 20%, the bottom of the watch band, because every amplifier that drove the morning fade is now decaying at once: the Nasdaq-100 cash index is 30,365.11, down only 0.14%, holding about 90 points above the 30,274.65 session low it rejected; VIX has rolled off its 17.59 session high to 16.99; the 10-year Treasury yield has eased to 5.248% from a 5.338% peak; and WTI is $91.72 against $92.61 an hour ago. Stress stays high at 76% on a 622-point NQ range and a rates channel still at 24-year highs.
recommendation: Tail moves to 20%, the lower edge of the watch band. The decisive observation is that de-escalation is now simultaneous rather than partial: an hour ago price had retraced its new session low while VIX sat at its session high and the 10-year was still near 5.30%, which was conflicting evidence. In this hour volatility, rates and crude are all easing together while price holds well above the rejected low, which is the orderly price discovery and cross-asset stabilisation this contract treats as grounds for Tail to fall. The environment nonetheless stays difficult, so Stress remains 76%: the NQ session range is 622 points, VIX is still 3.98% firmer on the day, Brent is $100.95 and the 10-year at 5.248% is close to its highest since April 2002. Confidence is 88% on fresh verified index, futures, yield, volatility and energy levels plus a verified release calendar. The danger window is narrowed to the current hour and the next while price remains below the 30,408.50 previous close.
headline: Tail eases to 20% as volatility, yields and crude all back off their highs together; Stress holds high at 76%
body: The Nasdaq-100 picture has improved again, and more cleanly than an hour ago. At the 15:26Z cutoff the evidence was genuinely conflicting: NQ futures had retraced about 106 points off a new 30,529.25 session low, but VIX was pinned at its 17.59 session high and the 10-year Treasury yield was still around 5.30%. At the 16:26Z cutoff that conflict has resolved in one direction. The cash index is 30,365.11, down 0.14% against a 30,408.50 previous close, holding roughly 90 points above the 30,274.65 session low and 211 points below the 30,576.44 high, so price sits mid-range rather than at an extreme. NQ futures are 30,613.75, down 0.28%, about 85 points above their 30,529.25 low within a 622-point daily range. Critically, the amplifiers are now decaying in parallel. VIX is 16.99, up 3.98% on the day but clearly off the 17.59 session high it held an hour ago, so volatility is decaying rather than expanding into the afternoon. The rates channel has faded further: the 10-year yield is 5.248% after easing more than four basis points from a 5.338% peak that was its highest since April 2002, with the 2-year at 4.80% and the 30-year back to 5.61%. Reporting attributes that relief to the ISM manufacturing survey pointing to a cooling in parts of the economy, which pulled shorter-dated yields down. Energy has also come in: WTI is $91.72, up 1.44% against 2.42% an hour ago, and Brent is $100.95, up 2.98% against 3.74%. Under this contract that combination - a rejected session low holding, volatility decaying, and yields and crude both retreating from their extremes - is the orderly, mean-reverting price discovery that permits Tail to fall, and it is why the score moves to the bottom of the watch band rather than staying mid-band. The macro inputs behind the session are unchanged and verified. The ISM Manufacturing PMI released at 14:00Z registered 54.5 against 54.6 in August and a consensus near 55, a ninth consecutive month of expansion, with New Orders 55.3, Production 56.7 and Employment 52.7. The market-moving component remains Prices at 77.9, up 6.8 points from 71.1, with respondents citing pricing volatility, tariffs, the Iran conflict and extended lead times; that is the standing reason the rates channel stays sensitive even as it fades today. Earlier releases were consistent: initial jobless claims 197K, continuing claims 1,701K, the four-week average 200K, S&P Global Manufacturing PMI Final 55.9 and construction spending up 0.9%. Energy remains the main standing amplifier rather than a fresh shock. Brent moved above $100 on reports that PetroChina withdrew several gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes scheduled for October to preserve domestic inventories, tightening refined-fuel availability in a market already disrupted by the US-Iran conflict and the war in Ukraine, while outright crude shortage concerns eased as Saudi Arabia resumed loadings at Yanbu and Middle Eastern crude shipments approached pre-war levels. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic with transits far below pre-war volumes, but that is a persistent background condition rather than new escalation today, so it informs Stress and not Tail. At the single-name level the tape is mixed rather than one-way: Micron fell about 2% despite a record fiscal fourth quarter and fiscal-Q1 guidance above expectations, Alphabet failed to hold early gains after releasing its latest AI model, and Amazon, AMD, JPMorgan and Bank of America were lower, while energy outperformed and materials and real estate lagged. Conflicting leadership of that kind reduces directional conviction and therefore raises Stress rather than Tail. The September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October is the next scheduled catalyst and is carried in the event calendar; no outcome for it is assumed anywhere in this assessment, and under this contract its proximity raises conditional Stress into the extreme band around the release while conditional Tail stays capped one point below the block threshold. Taken together: Tail 20%, the bottom of the watch band and one point lower; Stress 76%, two points lower but still high; Confidence 88% on fresh verified levels across index, futures, rates, volatility and energy plus a verified calendar. Dominant mode stays mixed. The shared Finviz context file carried a 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z collection time, roughly 41 hours old, with a partial collection status and explicit warnings that its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, so it was treated as unhealthy under the inherited contract and contributed nothing to this assessment; all evidence above came from independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Claude published an unbroken watch-band regime with a single orange hour. Tail ran between 20% and 25%, touching the 25% block threshold once in the 06:00Z hour on a trend-up reading before easing back when that structure failed to persist, then rising to 24% in the 14:00Z hour as the US cash open reversed the overnight rally. Stress climbed from 72% to a window high of 78% in the last two hours, and Confidence held at 87-89% throughout. Dominant mode was mixed in 22 of the 24 hours. The window describes a market absorbing a high-rates, high-energy-price environment inside a wide range rather than trending through it, and this hour is the first in which Stress has turned lower against that baseline.
outlookSummary: The near path turns on whether the rejected 30,274.65 cash low continues to hold while volatility and yields keep decaying. Conditional Tail holds 20% for the current and next hour while the session low and the 30,408.50 previous close bracket price, eases to 19% through the thinner US midday, returns to 20% for the 19:00Z power hour on late-session continuation or reversal risk, then decays to 17-18% across the post-close and Asian hours as liquidity thins and the assumed regime becomes quiet consolidation. From the 05:00Z European handover the conditional path rebuilds to 20-22% on calendar proximity rather than observed structure, ahead of the September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October. For the release hour and the hour after it, conditional Stress moves into the extreme band at 81% while conditional Tail is capped at 24%, one point below the block threshold: under this contract surprise magnitude and forecast dispersion raise Stress, not Tail, until an observed path actually shows failed retracements and repeated extension. No release outcome is assumed anywhere in the forecast, and conditional Confidence decays from 88% to 75% across the horizon to mark the widening gap between observed and projected evidence.
